predecessors.name: Second Spanish Republic
predecessors.text: the Nationalist zone of 1936, taken from the Republic by the rising of 17 to 19 July 1936: Spanish Morocco, the Canary and Balearic islands, Old Castile, León, Galicia, Seville and Cádiz (Spanish…

successors.name: Francoist Spain
successors.text: the whole of Spain after the Nationalist victory, declared by Franco on 1 April 1939

ledger.x: 1936: the generals rise against the Republic.
18 July 1936: the Army of Africa rises.
1936: Franco and Goded take the islands.
July to October 1936: the rebel zone on the mainland.
31 March 1937: the Nationalist offensive in the north opens.
21 October 1937: Gijón falls and the north is lost.
21 October 1937: the northern campaign ends with the whole coast in Nationalist hands.

1938: the rest of the growth of the Cliopatria shape between 1936 and 1938, in Andalusia, Extremadura and the Madrid sector (gazetteer overlay of the 1938 against the 1936-37 shape: Málaga 92 against under 2 percent, Huelva 95 against under 2, Toledo 64 against under 2, Badajoz 77 against 4, Madrid 66 against 9…
15 April 1938: the Nationalists reach the Mediterranean at Vinaròs.
19 April 1938: the offensive is 'for all intents and purposes concluded'.
1 April 1939: the Nationalist state becomes Francoist Spain.

wars.name: Spanish Civil War
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: 'Franco entered the capital and declared victory on 1 April 1939'.

wars.name: War in the North
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: Bilbao 19 June, Santander 26 August, Gijón 21 October 1937.

wars.name: Aragon Offensive
wars.outcome: Nationalist victory: the sea is reached at Vinaròs on 15 April 1938 and the offensive is concluded on 19 April.

certainty.note: Civil-war front lines, moved by campaigns and not fixed by any treaty; the northern provinces and the Aragon front are dated by the pages, the other lines by Cliopatria's shapes only.
